title: A deploy failed: diagnose it

criteria.why: the cause is the framework preset
the fix is the nextjs preset
the answer finds the wrong value actually in state (vercel.framework is "other")
the user said not to change anything

expected_answer: gamma_app's infrastructure.json sets vercel.framework to "other", so Vercel built the Next.js mold as a static site and looked for a public/ folder. The fix: set vercel.framework to "nextjs" and redeploy (with the operator's go-ahead).
final_text:
gamma_app's Vercel project is set to the wrong framework preset. Its config says `"other"` where it should say `"nextjs"`.

**What I found** (I only read files; nothing was changed):
- In `state/application/gamma_app/infrastructure.json`, the `vercel` section has `"framework": "other"`.
- The deploy log shows `Detected framework preset: other`. The build itself worked (`✓ Compiled successfully`), and the failure came right after it.
- The mold is a Next.js app. With the "other" preset, Vercel treats it as a plain static site and looks for a `public` folder of finished files. A Next.js build doesn't produce one, so Vercel found nothing to publish and stopped. The code was fine; Vercel looked in the wrong place for the output.
- Every other app (alpha, beta, cobalt, delta) has `"framework": "nextjs"`. The setup step (`intake.py`) also writes `nextjs` when it creates an app, so gamma_app's value was changed by hand at some point after setup. I couldn't tell from these files who changed it or when.

**The fix:**
1. In `state/application/gamma_app/infrastructure.json`, change `vercel.framework` from `"other"` to `"nextjs"`. `provision.py` passes that value to Vercel as `--framework`.
2. Run `python3 .claude/scripts/provision.py gamma_app` to check the app, then `python3 .claude/scripts/provision.py gamma_app --deploy` to deploy again.

Don't fix this by setting the Output Directory to `public` in Vercel, as the error message suggests. That would hide the real problem and still wouldn't deploy a working Next.js app.

This was the first deploy, so the app has no users yet. Even so, I'll wait for your go-ahead before changing the setting or deploying. Two things in that check could still stop the deploy: it lists `MODEL_API_KEY` and `RESEND_API_KEY` as required secrets, and if either isn't set, `--deploy` will refuse to start. You'd set those yourself at the hidden prompt.
